items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — The Science of the Seasons in 4 Points. Before discussing *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, Andrea Orlando's second album, it might be helpful to review the following preliminary points:1. The Bands. Andrea Orlando is the drummer on all four albums by La Coscienza Di Cena, an RPI band founded in Genoa in 2007, which released a superb self-titled debut album in 2011 and three other highly recommended albums between 2013 and 2018. Is it worth noting here that Genoa (Genova) is the birthplace of the illustrious PFM, one of the founding fathers of Italian progressive rock (RPI)?Before the formation of La Coscienza Di Cena, Andrea Orlando had already gained some recognition in this microcosm as a member of what it's fair to call the "Zuffanti nebula"?a transalpine prog music collective that began to coalesce around the Genoese bassist Fabio Zuffanti in the early '90s and gained greater visibility with Finisterre's debut album (1995).2. The Artist. Andrea Orlando joined Finisterre as early as 1997 on their *Live at Progday* and then on the fabulous *In Ogni Luogo* (1999), before returning for the 2019 comeback album. Orlando also played drums on *Mirrogames* (1998) by H�stsonaten, Zuffanti's other major band. In both cases, Orlando replaced Marco Cavani. To round out this overview, it's worth noting that drummer Andrea Orlando also contributed to the album by La Curva di Lesmo (2015), a duo that Zuffanti formed with Stefano Agnini, one of the two keyboardists on La Coscienza. And that brings us partially full circle.Let's now turn to the album itself by going over the other two points:3. The musicians. Since Andrea Orlando is one of the stalwarts of this famous Genoese music scene, it's no surprise that for his two solo albums, he called on other members of that same scene. For example, to give credit where credit is due, Zuffanti himself plays bass on one track from *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, and Boris Valle (Finisterre's longtime keyboardist) plays piano on another. Orlando, an accomplished drummer but also a capable keyboardist (with a predilection for the mellotron and organ), here cedes the piano parts?in addition to Valle?to Luca Scherani (H�stsonaten, La Coscienza di Zeno, La Curva di Lesmo) and to Agostino Marco (Finisterre, La Maschera, Zaal) for the Moog solos.On *Dalla Vita Autentica*, Andrea Orlando's previous solo album, the majority of the electric guitar parts were performed by two highly talented musicians: Marcella Arganese?who can be found in Ubi Maior and who regularly dazzles us with *Samura� of Prog*?and Laura Marsano, whom we've seen on Zuffanti's solo albums and those of drummer Maurizio Di Tollo. Two women on guitar?and not just any women?is rare enough to be worth noting, whatever the critics of "wokism" may say. On *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, Marcella has been replaced by Stefano Marelli, but Laura Marsano is always there to treat us to her poignant solos (the slow "Stagione Lontana"). The young singer Meghi Moschino contributes her calm, medium-toned voice to five of the seven tracks?a voice that reminds me a bit of Laura Mombrini's (Prowlers). On *Dalla Vita Autentica*, the robust vocals of Alessandro Corvaglia (another essential, ubiquitous figure on the RPI scene for several years), paired with those of Simona Angioloni (remember *Aries*, the band formed in the 2000s with? Zuffanti, him again), gave the whole a more robust feel. A matter of taste.4. The music. *La Scienza delle Stagioni* alternates between dynamic, vibrant tracks rooted in PFM's sun-drenched RPI, and tenderly romantic moments that unfold into expansive, emotionally charged symphonic prog, closer in style to *Hostsonaten*. By elegantly blending these two styles, the diptych "Il Sogno di Anastasia" (12:12) stands out as one of the album's most compelling tracks. In addition to "Il Sogno di Anastasia ? Parte Seconda," a lovely musical reverie with enchanting undertones, the album includes another instrumental, "City 40" (6:36), a sort of high-energy Latin version of "Samurai of Prog."The influence of Camel, noticeable from the very start of the previous album ("Le Forme Della Distanza"), is less pronounced throughout *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, giving way to more personal ideas, resulting in a kind of symphonic neo-prog with strong RPI influences. On the other hand, the extensive and frequent use of the mellotron (the long intro to "Stagione Lontana" with its celestial tones, or that of "La Strada del Ritorno," among others) draws the most serene moments toward the most ethereal Scandinavian prog.Of roughly similar length, the epic closing track, the highly symphonic "La Strada del Ritorno" (15:01), can be compared to the thrilling "Dalla Vita Autentica" (16:52), which closed the 2017 album of the same name, illuminated by an unforgettable solo by Marcella Arganese. But despite some structural and musical similarities, the comparison ultimately favors the latter, which is more ambitious and features more inspired melodies. Yet the melancholy that envelops the final section of "La Strada del Ritorno"?enhanced by Meghi's angelic voice and the serene appearance of the English and French horns?ultimately moves us, giving us the impression that a pale winter sun has come to breathe its loving breath upon us.At first glance, *La Scienza delle Stagioni* seems a little less striking than its predecessor, *Dalla Vita Autentica*. At the very least, it builds on its predecessor's strengths while retaining all its qualities, though without reaching quite the same heights. But let's not be fooled by first impressions. There are prog albums that possess a kind of natural clarity, made up of music whose beauty is immediately apparent; and others, like *La Scienza delle Stagioni*, that save their magic for a little later, revealing it just after we've finished listening, when we think we've moved on to something else. But that is the secret art of these mysterious works: to prepare for us an immediate future more beautiful than expected. *La Scienza delle Stagioni* possesses that special magic that fairies bestow as they lean over the cradle of certain works?a magic that stays with you and illuminates your path long after the notes have faded away.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评以四个层次的背景信息展开：首先介绍鼓手Andrea Orlando在热那亚前卫摇滚圈的人脉网络，特别是La Coscienza Di Cena和Finisterre等乐团的合作经历；其次梳理他个人的音乐生涯轨迹；再详细列出参与本张专辑录制的乐手阵容，包括Zuffanti、Valle、Scherani等圈内人物，以及女性吉他手Laura Marsano等。乐评结构偏重人物谱系而非音乐本体分析，对器乐编制和风格演变着墨较多，对专辑本身的作曲理念、声音设计或情感表达缺乏深入讨论。作为意大利前卫摇滚的圈内人作品，创作和演奏水准值得肯定，但风格上更偏向传统流派内的延续，较少触及实验或跨界元素。

items.body: Review by Finnforest — "After the Darkness, the Light" On their third and final album of the 1970s, Salis flipped the script once again, sounding nothinglike their previous effort five years prior. The Salis brothers were back, but they had a newdrummer and keyboardist in the lineup, and they obviously were hell-bent on forging a new direction.There is no sign of the debut's personality or the acoustic mellow vibe of the second. Here the bandhas shifted to that largely instrumental spacey fusion sound so common in the late '70s. The first reference that jumped into my mind was PFM's "Jet Lag" album, and I wondered if that wasan influence for Salis here, though "Jet Lag" is more adventurous than this. The mix of polishedrhythm section and quirky keyboard parts also reminded me just a bit of some of the instrumentalinterludes on later Cat Stevens albums. Another band this reminds me of is Finch. If you were intothem, you should enjoy these competent but sometimes tedious instrumentals. There are some very coollead guitar passages in several tracks. I suspect the approach is the reason why this album is ratedso much higher than their previous two, but frankly I don't see it. Yes, the longer jams overfloating keyboard atmosphere is going to appeal to progressive rock fans, but I think thecompositions on the first two albums are more interesting to me. Nevertheless, it is withoutquestion another good album by Salis. It all comes down to your tastes, naturally. I find this albumcompetent but pretty forgettable.
items._genre: rock progressivo italiano / fusion / instrumental progressive
items._cn_summary: 这是意大利Salis乐队1979年发行的第三张也是最后一张七十年代专辑。在更换鼓手和键盘手后，乐队彻底告别了首张专辑的个性表达与第二张的原声舒缓氛围，转向七十年代末常见的器乐主导型太空融合风格。乐评将其与PFM的《Jet Lag》以及Finch乐队相比较，但指出本作在冒险性上不及前者。专辑以抛光节奏部与古怪键盘线条交织为骨架，间或穿插出色的领奏吉他段落，呈现出漂浮键盘氛围之上的较长器乐即兴延展。尽管乐评承认这是乐队又一张合格作品，但整体评价倾向于'胜任却易遗忘'，认为前两张作品的作曲反而更具吸引力。对于偏好实验前卫与即兴融合的听众而言，这张专辑具备一定器乐探索价值，但在独特性与冒险性方面略显保守，属于融合范畴内的常规表达。

items.body: Soft Riot has finished a video for “Ghostwriter,” the closing track on the 2026 album “Crux.” It is the project’s second official video from the record, following “Moving Out Of The Black,” which premiered at the end of April 2026 ahead of the album’s release on 15 May. A premiere date for “Ghostwriter” itself is still being finalised; the video is not yet public. Crux by Soft Riot Jack Duckworth, who records as Soft Riot and is also known as JJD, built the video’s visuals as a graphic, surrealist collage rather than a straight performance piece, with puppet-like character animation reflecting the song’s theme: the sense of ideas for “Crux” materialising, as though something unseen were “ghostwriting” the record. All of the animation was made by hand from physically printed graphics and re-filmed projected textures, a deliberate move away from computer-based tools that Duckworth has linked to feeling increasingly isolated within the digital side of underground music. Duckworth handled all graphics and editing as JJD, with assistance from Leyre Mann Vadillo. “Ghostwriter” closes a nine-track album written and recorded across several sessions between June 2024 and January 2026 at Studio Carillon in Glasgow, with vinyl mixing by Owen Pratt at Flesh And Bone Studios in Tarn, France, and mastering by Josh Stevenson at Otic Mastering. “Crux” is available on streaming platforms, as a download through Bandcamp and Subvert via Possession Records, and on vinyl and digipak CD, including a limited clear vinyl LP on Minimal Kombinat that sold out within a week of pre-orders. A follow-up EP, “Alter,” released in June 2026, carries exclusive, alternate and extended versions of “Crux” material. About Soft Riot Soft Riot is the synth project of Jack Duckworth, a British-Canadian musician based in Glasgow who has released music under the name for around fifteen years, drawing on synth post-punk, darkwave, new wave, Italo and EBM. Duckworth’s roots go back to the mid-1990s art-punk and hardcore scene on the North American west coast, where he played in the first-wave post-punk revival band Radio Berlin (1998-2005) and the industrial synth-punk group A Luna Red (Gold Standard Labs, 1999-2003). As Soft Riot, he has toured Europe repeatedly, sharing stages with acts including Front 242, Absolute Body Control, Parade Ground, She Past Away, Test Department, Selofan, Drab Majesty and Lebanon Hanover, and has played festivals including Ombra Festival in Spain, BIM Fest and Waveteef in Belgium, Kalabalik På Tyrolen in Sweden and Weird Science in Germany. Side-Line has previously covered the Soft Riot albums “You Never Know What Might Come Next” (2016), “The Outsider In The Mirrors” (2018) and “When Push Comes To Shove” (2019), followed by “No.” (2023) and, in 2026, “Crux” and its “Alter” companion EP.
items._genre: synth post-punk / darkwave / EBM / new wave
items._cn_summary: Soft Riot 由英国-加拿大音乐人 Jack Duckworth 主导，这是其2026年专辑《Crux》完成第二支MV的消息稿。专辑共九首曲目，跨越2024至2026年在格拉斯哥 Studio Carillon 完成录制，混音与母带分别在法国和英国的工作室处理，发行涵盖流媒体、Bandcamp下载、黑胶及限量透明胶等多种形式。MV 视觉采用手工拼贴与定格动画方式，以物理印刷图形和重新拍摄投影纹理构成，拒绝电脑工具，体现对数字地下音乐环境的疏离感。Duckworth 音乐根基可追溯至上世纪九十年代北美西海岸的后朋克与硬核场景，后转向合成器路线，融合后朋克、暗潮、EBM、Italo 等元素，长期在欧洲地下舞台活跃。内容为厂牌/媒体新闻通讯，缺乏深度乐评分析。

items._cn_summary: 这是一支四人乐队在主流厂牌发行的首张完整专辑，以全篇统一的另类摇滚姿态呈现。作品中融入后朋克的锐利声响质感，同时穿插带有颜文字式松弛歌词的曲目，形成节奏与情绪上的反差。歌曲结构注重简约与空隙感的运用，吉他声墙与急促人声交替制造听觉冲击。抒情主线围绕即便希望微弱也选择向前的主题，呼应她们自身在创作中的心路历程。整体专辑在主流发行框架内保持了独立另类的审美取向，声音风格具有明确的日本地下乐队气质，对喜欢后朋克和另类摇滚交叉地带的听众具备一定吸引力。

items._cn_summary: 本文为The Wire电台节目单汇总，涵盖多张实验性音乐作品，横跨世界音乐、前卫即兴、地下独立等多个领域。曲目包括芬兰Svart厂牌发行的Harju黑胶原声带、Analog Africa重发的索马里Dur-Dur Band档案录音、Bill Orcutt的吉他独奏作品、橙牛奶厂牌的Ervin Omsk、Ak'chamel的环境即兴嘉宾混录，以及Carl Stone的电子音乐改编版本。选曲横跨萨米民间音乐、中东实验、非洲城市流行、先锋电子与无调性即兴，展现The Wire一贯的宽口径策展风格。整体为节目推介性质，缺乏深度乐评文字，但曲目编排本身反映了地下独立厂牌的当代图景。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A surprisingly-sophisticated and highly-entertaining album from a group of University of Illinois college students! Released on Brunswick Records in July of 1972.1. "The Monster Bride" (10:36) a very proggy, early King Crimson and Yes-like opening of bass, organ, clarinet, and delicate cymbal play turns in the second minute toward proggy brass rock--more like ELP meets BS&T. In the third minute the motif starts to smooth out before suddenly switching direction toward more light and playful circus music and then, in the fourth minute there is an equally sudden directional change toward more avant/eclectic Jazz-Rock Fusion before going Crimson and Zappa in the fifth. This is all quite tightly-performed and very sophisticated and unpredictable! It must have been something to compose and then pull off as a band in 1970s studio conditions. By the time we get to the end of the sixth minute everything slows down to a cymbal-supported droning organ for a Peter Hammill-like male vocal to enter and sing. Very Crimsonian! Flute and piano pick up from here with a very pretty, almost CHICAGO-like melody presentation and passage which builds and builds, horns entering and gathering forces over bass, guitar, and drum's rhythm track. At 5:22 everything stops for some percussion-backed dramatic very theatric narration of a sexually-piqued scene of the monster's reaction and response to the birth of his bride and child--which then leads to a finishing burst of CHICAGO-like brass rock. Very interesting! The sophistication of the compositions (and ability to pull it off in the studio) is the most impressive part. (18.375/20) 2. "Spiders (In Neals Basement)" (5:57) an accented male voice singing a sly lyric of film noir's detective-type music, like musical themes for scenes in a New Orleans juke joint or Chicago flop house. The music, performances both instrumentally and vocally are so colorful and spry. Great brassy theater music and great entertainment! Amazing that these were just a bunch of college kids! (9.333/10)3. "Witches Theme And Dance" (9:47) a brass rock song that opens like a LIGHTHOUSE song with great pace and energy before dropping down into a slow, plodding motif over which the gang issue some great four-part vocal harmony vocals. These guys must've done music theater or high school theater music. Bassist Neal Rosner is quite impressive (and, thankfully, placed forward in the mix), sounding a lot like Goblin or PFM's bassists. More stunning theatric stop-and-start composition performed with ease and professional precision over/within which electric guitar, voices, slide flute, and other mildly scary Hallowe'en noises contribute their solos and incidentals. Nice trilly flute solo in the final third--augmented by awesome "distant" flugelhorn. The finish is just perfect for the "lesson" of the witchy allegory. Another gem of a song; these guys are so creative and so talented! (18.875/20)4. "A Brief Message From Your Local Media" (9:59) here the band conjures up a four-part suite. It opens sounding like something from Aaron Copeland before organ, bass, hi-hat & bass drum lay down a soft carpet for a lone vocalist to begin his GREG LAKE-like "In the Court of the Crimson King" imitation. Obligatory flute joins in as "Greg" reaches his third verse--arpeggiated guitar chords and increasingly MICHAEL GILES-like drumming, as well. Around 4:30 there is a break in which narrator delivers a brief spoken-word summation of the contributions of Henry Ford to the workings of modern society, which is then followed by the development of a new motif of rather up-tempo organ- and flute-driven Jazz-Rock--which gains Latin elements in the eighth minute to give it a LEONARD BERNSTEIN West Side Story feel but then about a minute later the music moves more toward a pop/theatric-Brass Rock form similar to the snarky Hair, Godspel, and Pippen phenomenons. The music ends with a fading out calliope and military drums sound. Interesting. Though still delightfully creative and astonishingly sophisticated, the cohesiveness of this one is questionable (but, then, so is the flow of the typical radio or television programming!). (18.125/20) - a) "The Garden"- b) "The Assembly Line"- c) "Electric Man"- d) "Question"Total time 36:19Jazzy, brassy Crimsonian prog rock that sounds quite mature for a bunch of Illini students--and it's so entertaining, even addictive! Incredible for a debut album.A/five stars; a surprisingly-sophisticated and well-polished display of delightfully-entertaining compositions and performances. Who knew?! And, Whatever happened to?

items._cn_summary: 这张1972年专辑由伊利诺伊大学的学生乐团录制，展现出远超其年龄的作曲成熟度。首曲《The Monster Bride》时长超过十分钟，在前卫摇滚、爵士融合、ELP式铜管摇滚、马戏团音乐和先锋爵士之间频繁切换，中间穿插戏剧化的旁白段落，编曲复杂度令人印象深刻。第二首带有新奥尔良爵士乐与黑色电影配乐的气质，铜管编排活泼生动。第三首回归铜管摇滚路线，四部合唱配合贝斯主导的低音线，融合Hallowe'en式的怪诞氛围与精致的器乐solo。整体而言，这是一张将七十年代早期爵士摇滚、前卫摇滚与剧场音乐元素结合的融合作品，在风格实验性上有所建树，但核心仍偏向传统器乐摇滚谱系，与用户偏好的电子、实验、当代古典等方向交集有限。

items.body: Depeche Mode, the English electronic band from Basildon, Essex, released “Some Great Reward” on 24 September 1984 through Mute Records. The album turns 42 this year. It was the band’s fourth studio album, and it reached number 5 on the UK Albums Chart and number 3 in West Germany. Most of the record was made in West Berlin. Sessions began at London’s Music Works studio and moved to Hansa Mischraum, where the band also mixed the album. Daniel Miller produced it with Depeche Mode and Gareth Jones, who had engineered the previous record and was promoted to co-producer here. The band carried over the sampling approach it had started on Depeche Mode’s ‘Construction Time Again’, building rhythms from struck metal and concrete rather than drum machines alone. Martin Gore wrote eight of the nine songs; Alan Wilder contributed “If You Want”, the last song he wrote for a Depeche Mode album. Dave Gahan sang lead throughout, with Gore taking the vocal on “Somebody”, recorded live with Wilder on piano. The nine-track album runs “Something to Do”, “Lie to Me”, “People Are People”, “It Doesn’t Matter”, “Stories of Old”, “Somebody”, “Master and Servant”, “If You Want” and “Blasphemous Rumours”. Mute had issued “People Are People” as the lead single on 12 March 1984, six months ahead of the album, followed by “Master and Servant” on 20 August 1984 and the “Blasphemous Rumours” / “Somebody” double A-side on 29 October 1984. Both later singles drew objections over their sexual and religious subject matter, and some radio stations declined to play “Master and Servant”. Brian Griffin photographed the sleeve at Round Oak Steelworks near Stourbridge, continuing the industrial imagery he and designer Martin Atkyns had used on the previous cover. The album title is a line from “Lie to Me”. The Some Great Reward Tour opened three days after release and ran to the end of July 1985, taking the band through the UK, Europe, North America and two shows behind the Iron Curtain, in Budapest on 23 July and Warsaw on 30 July 1985. The 14 December 1984 concert in Hamburg was filmed and issued as the band’s first live video, “The World We Live In and Live in Hamburg”. About Depeche Mode Vince Clarke, Martin Gore, Dave Gahan and Andy Fletcher formed Depeche Mode in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, taking their name from a French fashion magazine. The band signed to Daniel Miller’s independent label Mute Records and released the synth-pop debut “Speak & Spell” in 1981. Clarke left after that album to form Yazoo with Alison Moyet, and Gore became the band’s main songwriter. Depeche Mode continued as a trio for “A Broken Frame” (1982), then expanded to a four-piece when Alan Wilder joined for “Construction Time Again” (1983), the album that brought sampled industrial sounds and Gareth Jones into the band’s productions. “Some Great Reward” extended that partnership and gave the band its first US chart single, “People Are People”, which reached number 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1985 after a delayed run there. Mute followed the album with the compilation “The Singles 81>85” in October 1985, then “Black Celebration” (1986), “Music for the Masses” (1987) and “Violator” (1990), which produced “Personal Jesus” and “Enjoy the Silence”. Wilder left in 1995 after “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993), and the remaining trio released “Ultra” (1997), “Exciter” (2001), “Playing the Angel” (2005), “Sounds of the Universe” (2009), “Delta Machine” (2013) and “Spirit” (2017). Fletcher died in May 2022. Gahan and Gore released “Memento Mori” as a duo in 2023 and toured behind it, documenting the Mexico City dates in the concert film “M”. Forty-two years on, “Some Great Reward” remains the point at which the Berlin sessions, the sampling and the leather-and-steel visual language settled into the form the band carried through the rest of the decade.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是对Depeche Mode第四张录音室专辑《Some Great Reward》42周年的纪念性梳理，详述了1984年的制作背景：专辑大部分在柏林Hansa录音棚完成，制作人Daniel Miller与乐队及Gareth Jones共同操刀。延续了前作《Construction Time Again》的采样实验，将打击金属与混凝土的声响纳入节奏构建。Martin Gore创作了九首中的八首，Alan Wilder贡献了最后一首为其乐队创作的作品。歌词涉及性与宗教争议主题，电台曾拒绝播放部分单曲。巡演延伸至铁幕背后的布达佩斯与华沙。整体以信息性回顾为主，非深度乐评。

items.body: The Red Garland Quintet Featuring John Coltrane and Donald Byrd - Soul Junction (Prestige, 1960) Culinary writers frequently refer to comfort food. Soul Junction is my comfort music. I go to this album when I’m not in the mood to be blown away by wild flights of improvised fury or complex compositions or arrangements. This is an “end of an exhausting day” or a “reminder that maybe all will be well” kind of an album. I love the relaxed, bluesy feel of it. Listen to Garland’s piano on the opening title track. It’s pure bliss. George Joyner’s bass is understated perfection. The piano trio portion of the track goes on so long and is so hypnotic that you’re to be forgiven if you forget there’s a sax and trumpet still to come. Hey, there’s the saxophone. It feels like Trane was digging Garland’s playing and was dying to join in. Recorded in 1957, Trane hadn’t perfected his style yet. But his genius is right there to hear. He’s fantastic on Dizzy’s classic Birk’s Works . Donald Byrd doesn’t get much mention on this website, but I love a lot of his Blue Note music. He’s the perfect trumpeter for this session. Garland wisely gives the two of them lots of space to play, and they take every advantage of it. John Coltrane- First Meditations (For Quartet) ( Impulse!, 1977) As far as I’m concerned, A Love Supreme is the greatest jazz album of all time and Coltrane’s classic quartet the greatest group. First Meditations (For Quartet) is a beautiful piece of music and a fascinating document of a band just on the verge of transforming, both in terms of its personnel and its approach to music. (I prefer to say “transforming” to “ending”.) The first track, Love, clearly recalls A Love Supreme, as if that classic album is the starting point of this new music. Trane is stunning as always and McCoy is the perfect accompanist. The best track, Joy, is relatively calm and peaceful, until it isn’t. It begins as any number of other tracks from this quartet and then Trane sits out. He’s let the remaining trio play some (for this group) fairly straightforward piano trio music. But then he returns with an absolute roar, as if he wants to break constraints the rest of us can’t see. This is one of several places you can see the seams of the band starting to tear. It’s fascinating to hear. Much of this music was reconsidered on the subsequent album Meditations with Trane’s new group. A comparison of the two albums and the approach of two different groups to the material is fascinating, the second album justifiably being the more renowned of the two. But I find the first to be the one I keep returning to, as if I don’t want to say goodbye to this quartet. I genuinely love this album, but I had an ulterior motive for writing about it here. It gives me the opportunity to tell the story of the time I met Elvin Jones. He had been doing a drum demonstration and a line formed afterwards for autograph seekers. When I arrived at the front of the line, I barely refrained from doing “We’re not worthy”, but I did tell him how much his music meant to me and said I’d be honored if he’d sign this album. He took the CD booklet from me, looked at it and asked “Did I play on this?”. (I assume that since the album wasn’t released until 10 years after it was recorded, he never saw the album cover.) I showed him his name in the booklet, he laughed and signed it, making this album all the more special to me. Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._genre: hard bop / spiritual jazz / modal jazz
items._cn_summary: 这是一张合辑性质的纪念发行，收录了Red Garland五重奏1960年的《Soul Junction》与Coltrane 1965年录音、1977年发行的《First Meditations》。前者是典型的硬波普风格，钢琴三重奏部分绵长催眠，Garland的蓝调式触感配合Coltrane尚未成熟的次中音萨克斯和Donald Byrd的小号，空间舒展而克制。后者则是Coltrane经典四重奏走向自由即兴前的转型记录，《Love》延续《A Love Supreme》的灵性主题，《Joy》中Trane突然回归爆发出撕裂性的能量，四重奏内部的张力与过渡清晰可闻。乐评以个人化笔触串联两张专辑，提及偶遇Elvin Jones的经历作为延伸叙事，但文章在末尾被截断，信息不够完整。

items._cn_summary: 这是两位传奇吉他演奏家——前Genesis成员Steve Hackett与Marillion主音吉他手Steven Rothery——的合作专辑《The Roaring Waves》。两位以情感丰沛的演奏风格著称，他们的吉他线条在这张作品中激烈交织，时而碰撞对抗，时而温柔相随，形成层次丰富的音乐对位。整体编曲追求宏大叙事感，音色构建出想象中的大海原般辽阔壮阔的音景。专辑以纯器乐形式呈现，让听者沉浸于缓慢舒展的声波中。两位传奇吉他手的合作本身就具备相当吸引力，演奏技巧与情感表达力均有保障，适合偏好器乐摇滚及吉他艺术的听众欣赏。

items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

items.body: Review by greenpete — They made a startlingly confident beginning with their exuberant, minor-label debut, An Evening With Dando Shaft (no, not a live album). But Dando Shaft's high-water mark arrived with this, their sophomore LP (often called the "Carousel" album, and released on RCA's short-lived Neon label, which only issued 11 albums total). This record dispenses entirely with drums, plunging deeper into varied, lyrical progressive folk. Singer Polly Bolton, from the wonderfully named village of Leamington Spa, joined the boys to bolster their string intricacies with her breathy, Sandy Denny-esque voice. The debut was marred only by the awkward "The Cat Song," but on the Carousel album, there's really not a bad cut. The Bulgarian-rhythmic songs of dual guitarists Dave Cooper and Kevin Dempsey, and mega-instrumentalist Martin Jenkins, are consistently strong, with Jenkins' mandolin, flute, and fiddle shining here. His tune "Whispering Ned," about a gent who enjoys indulging in sugar cubes (and whom the band evidently knew) adds an imaginative twist to the canon of drug songs. The upbeat "Pass it On" is notable for its exuberant chorus about values that have, sadly, since gone out of style. But the real highlights are "Till the Morning Comes" and "River Boat." Both feature Bolton's angelic vocals, the former a wispy duet with Cooper graced by luscious, gently psychedelic flute (Jenkins) and tablas (Ted Kay); and the latter an utterly breathtaking, pastoral delight that conjures green, rural England in poem-song.Bolton would stick around for Lantaloon, a good but inessential album, then depart after tiring of feeling like a "guest" vocalist. So if you plan to only get one album by this highly underappreciated psych-folk band...take a ride on the Carousel.- greenpete
items._cn_summary: 这是英国乐队Dando Shaft的第二张专辑，彻底放弃了鼓的运用，专注于器乐编排与人声结合的前卫民谣路线。女主唱Polly Bolton轻柔、近似Sandy Denny的声线成为专辑核心，与双吉他手Dave Cooper和Kevin Dempsey以及多乐器演奏者Martin Jenkins的曼陀林、长笛、小提琴交织。Jenkins创作了关于糖块的小品《Whispering Ned》，为传统毒品歌曲题材注入诙谐想象力。专辑融合保加利亚节奏元素，吉他层次丰富，配以塔布拉鼓和柔和迷幻长笛，呈现出英格兰田园诗般的声景。从器乐编排和东方节奏元素来看有一定跨界意识，但整体仍属传统民谣框架内的发展，缺乏更激进的声音实验。评论详实具体，对每首曲目都有针对性分析。

items.body: In September 1827, Hector Berlioz saw the actress Harriet Smithson play Ophelia in a Paris production of Hamlet and fell hopelessly in love. When his letters went unanswered, he turned the obsession into music, completing a symphony in 1830 at the age of twenty-six. It was first performed at the Paris Conservatoire that December, without Smithson in the audience. She heard the revised work two years later, and in 1833 the two were married. The program follows a young artist through five scenes: a reverie, a ball, a day in the country, a march to his own execution and a witches’ sabbath. The last two are opium nightmares, and the woman he loves haunts every scene as a recurring melody, the idée fixe. In the finale her theme returns as a cackling parody on a shrill E-flat clarinet, and bells toll as the Dies irae rises from the depths of the orchestra. Recordings part company on the details: the repeats in the first movement and the march, the optional cornet in the waltz, the bells, and old instruments versus modern. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the 10 best recordings of Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique. Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Colin Davis Colin Davis gives the listener the whole score: Every repeat is observed, the march’s among them, and the waltz includes the optional cornet part. Davis tightens the drama one movement at a time, and even Berlioz’s oddest sonorities are made to count. The price is a certain restraint. The ball ends in good order rather than a whirl, and the last two movements are held on a tighter leash than the music invites. Complete and played with unbroken concentration, this 1974 recording is the natural place to start. Davis Amazon Presto Apple Boston Symphony Orchestra, Charles Munch Where Davis builds the symphony with steady care, Munch plays it as theater, and this 1962 recording is a touchstone for that raw intensity. The first three movements are ardent, but the real storm is saved for the last two. When it breaks, the march and the witches’ sabbath erupt in a frenzy that still startles, with the whole orchestra driven to the edge. His faster 1954 recording is fiercer still in places, but finer playing and sound tip the balance toward the later version. For Berlioz at his wildest, this is the one to hear. Munch Amazon Presto Apple Orchestre Révolutionnaire et Romantique, John Eliot Gardiner John Eliot Gardiner took his period orchestra into the hall where the symphony was first heard in 1830. He seated the musicians as their counterparts sat in that era, with the violins split left and right, and the 1991 recording still sounds like a discovery. It flows more easily than the period-instrument pioneer before it, and its dynamics stretch from a bare whisper to full force without the inner lines ever blurring. Both repeats are taken, and the optional cornet brightens the waltz. The dry room leaves little halo around the sound, and it is no more thrilling than the great modern-orchestra versions. What it offers instead is the orchestra Berlioz knew, in the very room where his symphony was born. Gardiner Amazon Presto Apple Paris Conservatoire Orchestra, Ataúlfo Argenta Every movement runs faster than usual in Ataúlfo Argenta’s 1957 recording, and the scenes cut past like a film reel run too fast. Argenta skips the first movement’s repeat but takes the march’s, and the playing is not always polished, with some unevenness in the brass. None of that dims the impetuous energy, which carries the whole symphony along like one long, breathless dream. Argenta Amazon Presto Apple French National Radio Orchestra, Thomas Beecham A shadow lengthens through this famous 1959 recording. Beecham takes the story entirely seriously, and his march to the scaffold starts slower than usual, so the threat builds before the procession picks up speed. It is a darker, more measured journey than Argenta’s headlong dash. Beecham leaves out the first-movement repeat, and his mono recording from two years earlier burns hotter. Yet the slow build here pays off in a witches’ sabbath that is truly chilling. Beecham Amazon Presto Apple Orchestre National de France, Leonard Bernstein Every mood swing in the score is played to the full in this 1976 recording. Leonard Bernstein drives the first movement hard, yet he means every one of its quiet, hymn-like closing chords. The waltz has a teasing charm, and the idée fixe drifts through it and is gone. The march to the scaffold is the core of it, a procession that moves the listener to pity. Bernstein’s first New York recording has a sharper edge, and the sound here lacks some depth, but the performance wears its heart openly from first bar to last. Bernstein Amazon Presto Apple Cleveland Orchestra, Pierre Boulez Here the symphony is heard, above all, as a symphony. Pierre Boulez keeps close to the composer’s tempo markings, and the shape of each movement stands out with rare clarity. The Cleveland Orchestra plays superbly, with gorgeous strings and every climax held in firm control, and the disc adds Tristia with the orchestra’s chorus. Compared with Munch, this is a cool performance that keeps its emotional distance from the story. What this 1996 recording offers instead is Berlioz’s design laid out in full view. Boulez Amazon Presto Apple Rotterdam Philharmonic Orchestra, Yannick Nézet-Séguin This 2010 recording turns the drama inward. If Munch’s Berlioz is a fever, Yannick Nézet-Séguin’s is a confession, with the story told from inside the artist’s head as memory and feeling. The country scene is gently drawn, and the distant thunder at its close is kept low. The march stays in proportion, and in the finale the horrors are more dreamed than seen. Anyone after theatrical terror should look elsewhere, but the searching, personal tone is the point, and the disc adds La mort de Cléopâtre, sung by Anna Caterina Antonacci. Nézet-Séguin Amazon Presto Apple Les Siècles, François-Xavier Roth Nearly three decades after John Eliot Gardiner’s period-instrument version, François-Xavier Roth and Les Siècles bring the instruments of Berlioz’s day back to this score, and daylight falls between the lines. Roth went back to the composer’s manuscript before recording, and he lets each episode breathe before the next begins. The country scene is spare and unhurried, its period oboe and cor anglais calling to each other in their own reedy colors. In the witches’ sabbath, the bells come from La Côte-Saint-André, where Berlioz was born. The textures trade weight for light, and the finale closes in with a steady tread rather than an explosion. This 2019 recording is a beautifully observed performance, with every page freshly considered. Roth Amazon Presto Apple San Francisco Symphony, Michael Tilson Thomas From its opening bars, Michael Tilson Thomas’s 1997 recording shows the San Francisco Symphony in dazzling form, its playing at once exact and impassioned. The slow country scene never drags, and the march swings between the hushed and the enormous. For all that power, the last two movements burn less fiercely than the first three. The disc adds two excerpts from Lélio, Berlioz’s sequel to the symphony, and a 2024 remaster brings the recording to Apple Music in Dolby Atmos. items.body: Clan of Xymox released the double A-side single “Broken Heart” / “Fire” on 23 September 2026 through Metropolis Records in North and South America and Trisol in Europe. It is the first new music from the darkwave and goth act since their 2024 album “Exodus”. Broken Heart / Fire by Clan of Xymox Clan of Xymox co-founder and frontman Ronny Moorings describes “Broken Heart” as “a journey through heartbreak, desire and emotional combustion.” Built on layered synth lines and a steady mid-tempo pulse, the track pairs Moorings’ vocal with lyrics about a relationship that will not fully end; his aim, he says, was “to capture the tension between losing someone and still being consumed by them.” A music video for “Broken Heart” is scheduled to go online later on 25 September, at 6pm UK time (7pm CET). No further details on “Fire”, the single’s second A-side track, were provided beyond its inclusion alongside “Broken Heart”. The single arrives as Clan of Xymox continue a run of live dates through the end of 2026, including main-stage slots at WGT-Leipzig and M’era Luna earlier in the year. Upcoming shows run from Italy in early October through Germany, Austria, Hungary, Croatia, Spain, Poland and France in November and December: 2 October – Traffic Club, Rome, Italy 3 October – Lizard Club, Naples, Italy 7 November – Gleis 9, Bochum, Germany 10 November – Strom, Munich, Germany 11 November – Chelsea, Vienna, Austria 12 November – A38, Budapest, Hungary 13 November – Culture Factory, Zagreb, Croatia 21 November – Sala Jerusalem, Valencia, Spain 27 November – Klub CK Wiatrak, Zabrze, Poland 5 December – La Laiterie, Strasbourg, France About Clan of Xymox Clan of Xymox formed in Nijmegen, the Netherlands, in 1982, when Ronny Moorings and Anka Wolbert began writing together as students. The pair relocated to Amsterdam and were joined by Pieter Nooten, and the group signed to the British label 4AD in 1985, releasing their self-titled debut album that year and “Medusa” in 1986. Their atmospheric, synth-driven post-punk sound built a cult following across the UK and mainland Europe during this period. The band moved to PolyGram’s Wing Records for “Twist of Shadows” (1989) and “Phoenix” (1991), shifting toward a more commercial synth-pop direction that incorporated alternative dance elements and brought them US chart exposure. Nooten and Wolbert left after “Phoenix”, and Moorings continued as the band’s sole constant songwriter through a run of independent releases in the early-to-mid 1990s. The group signed to Metropolis Records in North America in 1997 and to Trisol Music Group for European releases from 2009, distribution deals the band has kept ever since. The resurgence of interest in gothic and electro-industrial rock through the 1990s and 2000s gave Clan of Xymox a renewed audience, and the band has maintained a steady release and touring schedule in the decades since. Their most recent studio album, “Exodus”, arrived in mid-2024, followed by the “Blood of Christ” EP later that year and a 3CD edition of “Exodus” in early 2025. The band’s current touring line-up includes Moorings alongside Mojca Zugna, Mario Usai and Sean Winzer. “Broken Heart” / “Fire” is the group’s first new material since that run of 2024 and 2025 releases, and arrives alongside a fresh round of European festival and club dates through the end of 2026.
items._cn_summary: 本文为Clan of Xymox双A面单曲《Broken Heart》/《Fire》的发布新闻稿，介绍了单曲于2026年9月23日通过Metropolis Records和Trisol发行的信息。文中引用主创Ronny Moorings对《Broken Heart》的描述，称其探讨心碎、欲望与情感燃烧，以层叠合成器声部和中速律动构建张力，歌词围绕一段无法彻底结束的关系展开。该单曲是乐队继2024年专辑《Exodus》之后的首支新作，文章还列出了乐队2026年下半年的欧洲巡演日程。背景部分回顾了乐队自1982年于荷兰奈梅亨成立、签约4AD、转向商业合成器流行、成员变动并最终落户独立厂牌的历史脉络。作为暗潮/哥特领域的老牌乐队，Clan of Xymox的风格偏向成熟的类型化制作，缺乏显著的实验性突破或声音设计上的新意。文章本身属于资讯类新闻稿，缺乏深入的乐评分析。

items.body: Conscience, the German electropop and synthpop project of Rüdiger Illg, releases the compilation “Uncharted Vol. 1 (The Singles 2009-2023)” on Echozone on 25 September 2026. It gathers Conscience’s single releases from that period into one set, adds one new song and three new mixes, and presents every track remastered. The label describes a second volume, “Uncharted Vol. 2”, as already in the works. Despite the plural billing Echozone sometimes gives the project, Conscience remains a one-man operation: Illg writes, plays and produces every track himself at Science2, his home studio in Leeste, Lower Saxony. He formed Conscience in 1991, but “Uncharted Vol. 1” starts its clock at 2009, not at the project’s founding. Echozone explains why: Conscience did not sign a record deal until 1998, with the “Hardware” EP, and that contract proved short-lived. Illg then signed to Echozone, whose own account of the compilation dates that move to around 2008, when “Theatre Of Deception” served as the lead single for the album “Gravity Has Gone”; Side-Line’s earlier research into the project’s Echozone catalogue had put that signing a year later, in 2009. Physical releases stopped soon after over cost, and for years Conscience issued albums and EPs with no accompanying singles at all. That changed with the 2020 album “Sentient”, after which every Conscience album has carried multiple single releases, the run “Uncharted Vol. 1” now compiles. The compilation follows the single “Explain Everything”, which Echozone issued on 28 August 2026 as an advance taste of the same collection. About Conscience Rüdiger Illg founded Conscience in August 1991, working first with a single Yamaha SY22 synthesizer, and has written, played and produced every track since under that name at Science2. He also records as Science O.C.N. and Chaos Network. The project’s first six years produced cassette-only releases traded through the tape network, followed by a first CD in 1998 and a run of CD-Rs through the early 2000s. NewEx Records picked up Conscience in 2007, and Illg signed to Echozone in 2009, a relationship that has produced the bulk of the catalogue since, including the albums “Phases³” (2025) and “Suspended In Time” (2026) and the singles and EPs “Uncharted Vol. 1” now draws its selections from. Guest vocalists across the catalogue have included Colin Angus of The Shamen and Dan Söderqvist of Twice a Man. “Uncharted Vol. 1 (The Singles 2009-2023)” is Conscience’s first compilation to collect that stretch of the catalogue in one release, with a second volume already planned.
items._cn_summary: Conscience是德国单人电子项目，由Rüdiger Illg自1991年起在家中录音室Science2独立完成词曲、演奏与制作。即将发行的《Uncharted Vol. 1》是2009至2023年间单曲作品的首次合集，附带一首新曲与三首新混音，所有曲目经过重新母带处理。这是一篇典型的厂牌发行资讯，内容侧重于项目历史梳理、签约脉络与实体唱片变迁，几乎没有涉及音乐本身的创作手法、声音设计或美学评价。该项目定位为合成器流行与电子流行，长期合作Echozone这一专注暗潮与电子领域的独立厂牌，客座歌手包括The Shamen的Colin Angus和Twice a Man的Dan Söderqvist。文本偏向信息汇编而非深度乐评。

items.body: Front Line Assembly released their eighth studio album, “Hard Wired,” through Off Beat on 25 September 1995, with Metropolis Records handling North America and Energy Rekords issuing the record in Sweden. It was the Canadian electro-industrial band’s first release for the German label. The album turns 31 this year. Bill Leeb and Rhys Fulber produced the record and wrote all ten tracks, which run 62 minutes: “Neologic Spasm,” “Paralyzed,” “Re-Birth,” “Circuitry,” “Mortal” (instrumental), “Modus Operandi,” “Transparent Species,” “Barcode,” “Condemned” and “Infra Red Combat.” Greg Reely engineered and mixed, with Delwyn Brooks assisting, continuing a working partnership that began on “Caustic Grip” in 1990. Devin Townsend played electric guitar, returning after his session work on the previous year’s “Millennium.” Dave McKean produced the illustration, design and photography. The sessions ran roughly five months at the Warehouse. Leeb wrote the lyrics only once the music was finished, and described that order as the band’s normal method rather than a choice made for this record: “We write […] the music and then once we’ve got it finished, then I sit at home and start on the lyrics. I can’t imagine writing any other way. […] I think with our music it’s usually the sounds that inspire us.” On what those lyrics deal with, he set materialism and environmental collapse against the technology driving both: “I think most of the lyrics are basically about man versus technology. Basically, we’re destroying our planet with technology. At the same time, technology is the only thing that can save us. It’s this constant struggle between these two forces that is making us go in whatever direction we’re all going.” That reading runs through the sampling as well. The album draws audio from “True Romance,” “In the Mouth of Madness,” “Lifeforce,” “Stargate,” “Speed,” “The Puppet Masters,” “No Escape,” “Romeo Is Bleeding,” “The Crow,” “Lethal Weapon” and “Alien 3,” alongside sound effects from the 1993 video game “Doom” and passages from three Aphex Twin recordings. “Circuitry” was the album’s only single, released on 31 October 1995. Its limited edition came as a two-CD digipak with remixes by Haujobb and Biosphere, a mixed-mode first disc carrying the “Millennium” video and photo galleries, and a second disc with the non-album tracks “Destructive Transformation” and “Hydrogen.” The album reached number 47 on the Swedish albums chart and the single number 32 on the Swedish singles chart. “Hard Wired” has sold at least 50,000 copies worldwide, and its 5,000-copy limited edition sold out in two weeks. A further track from the same sessions, “Plasticity,” was held back and issued separately; Fulber explained the decision in commercial terms: “We kept it off the album to release later […] It gives people a reason to check it out because if you release it as a single that is already on album no one is really going to care.” The “Plasticity” video won Best Alternative Video at the MuchMusic Video Awards in Toronto in 1996. The album has returned to shelves twice since. Black Rain Records pressed a 500-copy picture vinyl in August 2011, cut to seven songs, dropping “Mortal,” “Modus Operandi” and “Transparent Species.” For the record’s twentieth year, Artoffact Records issued a 300-copy vinyl box in 2015 pairing the album with the “Live Wired” live record and the “Circuitry” single, all remastered by Reely; Side-Line reported that The Front Line Assembly 6LP boxset ‘Hard Wired’ is almost sold out that May, and covered the same year’s news that Front Line Assembly finally see ‘Plasticity’ released on a 10 inch vinyl (3 formats). “Hard Wired” streams on Spotify. About Front Line Assembly Bill Leeb formed Front Line Assembly in Vancouver, Canada, in 1986, shortly after leaving Skinny Puppy, where he had contributed bass synth and backing vocals between 1985 and 1986 under the name Wilhelm Schroeder. He picked the band name to reflect his view that strength lies in working together. The demo tapes “Nerve War” and “Total Terror” were limited to 100 copies each and mostly passed around among friends, with Rhys Fulber contributing as an unofficial member. The project’s first appearance on record was “Aggression,” on the 1987 Third Mind compilation “For Your Ears Only.” Belgian label KK issued the debut album “The Initial Command” at the end of 1987, with Fulber and Michael Balch assisting, and German label Dossier released “State of Mind” in January 1988. When a planned Nettwerk release fell through, Third Mind put out “Corrosion” and the “Disorder” EP later that year, then signed the band to a three-album deal and licensed “Corrosion” to Wax Trax! for North America. Balch became an official member in 1988 and left after the 1989 “Gashed Senses & Crossfire” tour to join Ministry and Revolting Cocks. Fulber replaced him and appeared on “Caustic Grip” (1990), the album that started the band’s long partnership with engineer Greg Reely and introduced guitar on “Provision” and “Resist.” Chris Peterson debuted as live percussionist on the tour that followed in early 1991. “Tactical Neural Implant” (1992) turned toward more melodic, multi-layered arrangements and the heavy film sampling that became a fixture of the sound. Five remixes for Fear Factory’s “Fear Is the Mindkiller” EP in 1993 fed directly into “Millennium” (1994), the band’s first industrial metal record, built on metal guitar samples and Devin Townsend’s session work. “Hard Wired” arrived the following September. Fulber left in 1997 to concentrate on production, and Peterson took his place for “FLAvour of the Weak” (1997), “Implode” (1999) and “Epitaph” (2001), a run that traded the metal influences for breakbeat and big beat. Fulber returned for “Civilization” (2004), and Peterson rejoined for “Artificial Soldier” (2006), the first album to feature Jeremy Inkel and Jared Slingerland. “Improvised Electronic Device” (2010), “Echogenetic” (2013), “Wake Up the Coma” (2019) and “Mechanical Soul” (2021) followed, the last on Metropolis. The band also composed soundtracks for the games “Quake III: Team Arena,” “AirMech” and “WarMech.” Inkel died on 23 January 2018 at the age of 34, from complications of an asthma condition. Leeb has run Delerium since 1987 and Noise Unit since the late 1980s, while Fulber started Conjure One after his 1997 departure and has worked with Fear Factory for decades; Side-Line published a Front Line Assembly interview – Catching up with Bill Leeb and Rhys Fulber in 2024. “Hard Wired” turns 31 this year, the record that closed out the guitar-driven stretch the band opened with “Millennium” before the electronics took over again.
items._cn_summary: 此文为Front Line Assembly第八张录音室专辑《Hard Wired》发行31周年的回顾性新闻稿，重点介绍了专辑的制作背景与发行信息，而非真正意义上的乐评。文章罗列了十首曲目的标题、录制周期、制作人员与厂牌细节，强调Bill Leeb与Rhys Fulber延续先曲后词的创作流程。专辑通过大量电影采样构建叙事感，配乐取材自《True Romance》《The Crow》及Aphex Twin作品，电子游戏《Doom》的音效也被纳入。歌词聚焦于人类与技术的矛盾关系，涉及物质主义与环境崩塌等议题。该厂牌虽属独立运营，但此次发布未对音乐本体进行任何艺术层面的深度剖析，缺少音效、编曲、美学取向的评价，仅止于资料整理，无法提供聆听引导或审美判断。

items.body: Top PickThe Ocean – Solaris (progressive post-metal) Eden should be along with a proper review sometime in the near future, but it's safe to say this first outing from the new Ocean line-up is not only a bona fide success, but also stands out as one of their strongest albums to date. The jump in quality might not come as a surprise after the snoozefest that was Holoxene (2023), but there's an argument to be made that this is the best Ocean album since genuine GOAT-contender Pelagial (2013), or even outside of it.At well over an hour and with songs and song-suites pushing the ten, fifteen and even twenty-minute mark, Solaris can be a tall order. Likewise, its expansive and layered composition works best when played in full and paying it complete attention, which is probably why I haven't listened to it nearly as much as I should have, even though we've had the promo for a month or so now. Rest assured though, that this is an album I will be playing and referring back to for years to come, and I doubt I'm alone in that assessment. Solaris by The Ocean Last Week's Most Unjustifiably Overlooked ReleaseUncle Acid and the Deadbeats – Shapes of Midnight (occult rock/metal)I didn't give this one a proper listen before posting last week's roundup, we got the promo early, but, after a quick sample I wrote it off as a good album from a band I respected but traditionally Wasn't For Me™. I should have paid more heed to Jordan's review though, because—while I'm not qualified to comment on whether this is the best Uncle Acid and the Deadbeats album—I can say its doing a whole lot more for me than any of their previous records have, or similar releases of its ilk have been lately.In comparison to the shark-jumping self-parody of the new Green Lung record, Shapes of Midnight oozes class and sincerity, along with a compelling mastery of its craft. It also rocks super hard. Along with the expected malaize of psychedelic Black Sabbath worship that pervades their sound, "Psycho on the Loose" sounds like Turbonegro covering Turbo-era Judas Priest, while "Don't Let it Control You" almost sounds like Motorhead mixed with Hellhammer, with lots of bass fills that bring to mind "Born to Be Wild". Indeed, bassist Justin Smith may well be the man of the match, delivering a Meddle-esque Pink Floyd trudge on "When Evil Wakes" and plenty of Geezer Butler-isms throughout that help make Shapes of Midnight a surprisingly vital pre-summer soundtrack as the weather starts to get warmer down under. items._cn_summary: 本期内容为多张专辑的合辑式乐评。The Ocean的Solaris被列为本周首选，评论认为这是新阵容的首张正式作品，质量大幅超越前作Holoxene，可与后者并列为乐队最佳专辑；编曲层层铺陈，曲目长度多在十至二十分钟之间，适合完整专注聆听。Uncle Acid and the Deadbeats的Shapes of Midnight被定位为上周被忽视的作品，评论指出其在神秘摇滚框架下融合了黑色安息日式的迷幻崇拜、Judas Priest式的重金属冲击以及Motörhead式的贝斯驱动，贝斯手Justin Smith的表现尤为突出。其余专辑简介涵盖进步/工业黑金属、重金属、激流金属、交响金属、独立噪音摇滚、金属核以及葬礼末日金属等多种流派，但仅给出名称与类型标签，缺乏深入评述。整体偏重金属谱系内的常规评介，与实验、前卫爵士及电子等领域的距离较远。

items._cn_summary: 本文为日本神奈川县县民ホール主办的活动预告，介绍2026年9月在横滨举行的「AI与现当代音乐」专题活动。活动分两部分：第一部分为关于人工智能与现当代音乐的座谈会，邀音乐学者沼野雄司主持，安藤大地、徳井直生、中ザワヒデキ等作曲家与研究者参与讨论；第二部分为AI主题委约作品世界首演音乐会，由柴山真太朗、坂東祐大、向井響三位作曲家担纲。文章内容主要为活动信息与出席者介绍，未涉及具体音乐作品的音响描述、创作技法分析或艺术评价。涉及人工智能作曲与电子音乐等实验元素，但整体为新闻稿性质而非原创乐评。

items.body: 今週も世界中の最新ジャズニュースから気になるトピックをピックアップ。 サックスという楽器が抱えてきた振れ幅を、今週は何度も思い出させられる。コルトレーン生誕100年の節目、ブランフォード・マルサリスとダイアン・リーヴスの共演、ローランド・カーク晩年の実験、そしてアンディ・シェパードとジョーイ・アレクサンダーの新作。世代も国籍も異なる5つの動きを追う。 ブランフォード・マルサリスとダイアン・リーヴス、Blue Noteでの再会 ブランフォード・マルサリス・カルテットと、ヴォーカリストのダイアン・リーヴスによるコラボレーションアルバム『Dedicated To You』が、Blue Noteからリリースされた（UK Vibe誌のレビュー）。出典で確認できるのはブラックヴァイナル仕様と限定カラー盤の存在までで、CDでの発売については出典本文に記載がないため、ここでは触れない。 ブランフォードは、弟ウィントン・マルサリスと並び称されてきたソプラノ／テナー奏者で、2002年作『Footsteps of Our Fathers』でジョン・コルトレーンの『A Love Supreme』を完全収録した経緯を持つ人物でもある。一方のダイアン・リーヴスは、10代の頃にクラーク・テリーからスタンダード・レパートリーの手ほどきを受け、1977年には「カルデラ」への参加を経て、1987年にBlue Noteと契約した最初の歌手となった歌い手である。系譜の異なる二人が同じ盤の上で言葉を交わす構図に、このアルバムの聴きどころがある。 出典：https://ukvibe.org/album_reviews/branford-marsalis-dianne-reeves ローランド・カーク、晩年の「新しさへの追求」 マルチリード奏者ローランド・カークの晩年の意欲作『Slightly Latin』が、Jazz Journal誌のコラム「JJ 09/66」で改めて取り上げられている。トロンボーン奏者ギャレット・ブラウンとの共同編成のもと、ラテン音楽の要素を取り込み、カーク特有の角ばった音色をより柔らかく響かせようとした一枚だという。 本作の背景には、1960年代半ばのジャズシーンにラテン音楽の語彙が浸透していった時期の空気がある。カークがバリトン・サックスという新たな声を得ようとしていたことも、Jazz Journalの評は伝えている。同誌はこの模索を「新しさへの絶えない追求」と評した。   出典：https://jazzjournal.co.uk/2026/09/20/jj-09-66-roland-kirk-slightly-latin アンディ・シェパード、静謐に寄せる5作目 イギリスのサックス奏者アンディ・シェパードの5作目となる新作『Salt Catchers』が、ECMから発表された（UK Jazz News）。出典によれば、本作は伝統に根ざした叙情性と、音数を絞った静けさを湛えた一枚だという。 シェパードは、ピアニストのリタ・マルコトゥッリ、ベーシストのミシェル・ベニータら長年の共演者と再びこの一枚を作り上げた。出典によれば、シェパード自身はキャラ・ブレイの「Lawns」をこれまでライブでは演奏してきたが録音してこなかったといい、今回初めて本作で録音に収めたという逸話も紹介されている。ここでは、シェパード個人がこの叙情性とどう向き合ってきたかという、小さな一点に絞って触れておく。 出典：https://ukjazznews.com/andy-sheppard-salt-catchers ジョーイ・アレクサンダー、10歳で世界に見出された歩み ジャズピアニスト、ジョーイ・アレクサンダーを取り上げた評論記事が『UK Jazz News』に掲載された。バリ島出身の彼は、2014年、10歳でニューヨークに移り住んだ直後にその演奏がウィントン・マルサリスの目に留まり、そこから国際的なジャズシーンへ足を踏み入れた経歴を持つ。 「アジア発のジャズプレイヤーが国際的に認識される時代」という大きな見立てを、今回の出典1件だけで裏づけるのは難しい。ここでは、一人のピアニストがどこから歩き出し、誰に見出されたかという個人史の線を辿るに留める。 出典：https://ukjazznews.com/joey-alexander コルトレーン生誕100年の節目に ジョン・コルトレーンが生まれてから、今年で100年になる。NPRのジャズ評論欄では、この節目に寄せた論考が公開されている（NPR、2026年9月22日）。 今回参照できた素材は表題と概要のみで、論考本文の具体的な主張までは確認できていない。テナー・サックス奏者としての革新性については、出典本文を確認できた段階で改めて扱いたい。 出典：https://www.npr.org/2026/09/22/nx-s1-5976887/marking-the-100th-birthday-of-jazz-great-john-coltrane 投稿 【ARBAN WEEKLY ／今週の話題まとめ】コルトレーン生誕100年、そしてブランフォードとリーヴスの邂逅ほか は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。
items._genre: jazz / vocal jazz / latin jazz / contemporary jazz
items._cn_summary: 本篇文章是ARBAN周刊的爵士新闻汇总，涉及五个主题：布兰福德·马萨利斯与戴安·里夫斯在Blue Note合作的致敬专辑、罗兰德·柯克晚年融合拉丁元素的作品回顾、安迪·谢泼德在ECM发表的抒情新作、乔伊·亚历山大的个人经历介绍，以及约翰·柯川诞辰一百周年的纪念。内容以新闻摘要为主，缺乏深度评论，对各张专辑的制作细节、音乐结构与艺术取向着墨有限。其中柯克的拉丁爵士实验与谢泼德的ECM抒情路线略有跨界意味，但整体偏向主流爵士范畴，与实验、前卫、跨界融合等方向的关联度较低。

items._cn_summary: 这是尼日利亚歌手艾拉·斯塔尔的第三张专辑，迁居纽约后发行。专辑融合了哀愁风格的阿弗罗比兹节奏、拉丁系深度浩室、中东风味的舞厅音乐、雷昂·托马斯参与的合成器放克以及与泽恩合作的钢琴抒情曲等多种风格。其低音人声在各种曲风中均能贴合，呈现出多面向的强劲面貌。整体制作以全球化流行框架为主，风格虽然多元，但在实验性和声音设计层面并无突出突破。与追求前卫实验、深层即兴或极端声音美学的听众口味距离较远，更偏向主流跨地域流行融合的定位。

items.excerpt: すでに英米で高いチャート・アクションを見せている6年ぶりの新作。ジャック・アントノフら新たなコラボレーターを迎えて制作され、ヴォコーダー処理が夢想性を演出する“The Outside”やアンビエントなフォーキー・サウンドに包まれた “The Governor’s Waltz”、あるいはシューゲイズ的な音像の“Bobby”など多彩な曲調が取り揃えられ、いわば静謐さと激情が拮抗しながら独特の緊張感を醸し出しているが、その一方で全体として揺るぎないトータリティーが構築されているところに彼女の確かな成長の証を見る。大胆さと野心が音の隅々まで迸る、鮮烈なまでのサード・アルバムだ。

items._cn_summary: Phoebe Bridgers时隔六年推出的第三张专辑，邀来Jack Antonoff等新合作者参与制作。专辑在曲风上呈现多元化面貌：开场曲运用声码器处理营造梦境感，另一首浸于氛围化民谣音景中，也有作品采用瞪鞋摇滚式的音墙处理。整体在静谧与激烈之间维持张力，形成统一的听感结构，被视为创作者成长的体现。制作层面展现出明确的创作野心，声响设计在流行民谣的框架内进行了多向探索。

items._cn_summary: 这是一篇对作曲家兼多乐器演奏家韦斯顿·奥伦茨基的采访预告，而非专辑乐评。文中提到他在南卡罗来纳州成长、曾参加国际鼓乐队的经历，并将其重新审视为一种对帝国外战的音乐化演绎。他的工作聚焦于乐器的文化历史与音乐制作方式本身，涉及对行进音乐传统的批判性反思。作为驻扎在柏林的美国音乐人，他的创作处于当代古典与实验音乐的交汇地带，关注乐器本体及其社会文化语境。文章内容极为简短，仅为采访介绍，缺乏具体的音乐技法与作品分析，信息量不足以构成有效评价。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Despite having been around for some thirty years (their first album, released in 1993, was produced by Eroc, former drummer of Grobschnitt), very little has been written about this German band in the progressive music press, with the exception of a few wonderfully insightful reviews published in 2001 to mark the release of their masterpiece, *Fantasma*. In those insightful lines, everything was said?from the impeccable vocals of Oliver Philipps?the heart and soul of the band?which stir us with emotion in airy, nostalgic atmospheres, to Everon's distinctive taste for Rush at its most melodic. Incidentally, the influence of the fathers of Canadian hard-prog on a band from our good old continent is rare enough to warrant special mention. For good measure, among the similarities or influences more or less acknowledged by Everon, we should also mention the prog metal of Vanden Plas, the even more symphonic style of Sylvan, or the more neo-prog sound of Pallas. And despite my fear of intriguing or horrifying some readers, I'll also take the liberty of pointing out Oliver Philipps's avowed fondness (see his website) for Nik Kershaw.But it's through a subtle affinity for Rush that *North* really bursts onto the scene, with a mind-blowing and compact "Hands ", driven by an unstoppable melody yet free of any lulls or orchestral flourishes (here, a few keyboards with a discreet but essential presence)?exactly as Oliver Philipps intended, having momentarily had his fill of his own sumptuous arrangements.A track remarkable for its ability to encapsulate the very best of its creator's aspirations, "Hands" reassures us of Everon's intentions: to succeed in creating something that is both simple and grandiose. This is something the band's two previous albums, *Flesh* and *Bridge*?which were not substantial enough despite the extravagant 14-minute title track "Flesh"?partially failed to achieve; curiously, both were released in the same year (2002). The next track, "A Brief Encounter", is the biggest surprise on the new album: constructed like a sort of "Turn of the Century" in tune with our times (read: with a testosterone boost), complete with acoustic guitar and piano parts, it unabashedly reveals the depth of Philips' love for the universal sound of Yes. The greatest (and consistent) melodic shortcoming?at least on the early albums?has, over time, become a strength. Straight to the point: emotion. UnforgettableOliver is a tremendous singer who has never stopped improving since a debut album that was nearly disastrous in that regard (a young Greg Lake's voice, uncertain and poorly anchored to confusing melodies) to reach a level that only the very best have attained. On that note, on *North*, be sure to listen to "Test of Time", opulent prog metal with a brief cello intro. Or the tormented "North" ("I remember I wrote 'North' on an unbelievably stormy day" (O. Philipps), with its false string section richer than a cathedral door.Olivier Philipps is also an excellent musician (guitars, keyboards) who puts his performance at the service of the richness of the melody?and not the other way around. He's fairly sparing with solos but increasingly generous with pure emotion, as on "Wasn't It Good" (6:33), the most poignant track on *North*, my favorite track, and probably also Oliver Philipps's favorite on this album: "Actually, in my humble personal opinion, this kind of song is the essence of what Everon is all about" (O. Philipps). At the beginning, with a touch of nostalgia, a piano begins to float heavily through the ether, the melody detached from its harmonic body, a sphere of thought undulating at the end of a long string. And when the guitar solo comes in?which seems as simple as pie, so much so that even my thick, clumsy little fingers think they can play it?you find yourself hoping never to hear another lukewarm review of Everon.The edgy "Woodworks", a highly successful instrumental, as if to retrospectively disprove the famous review mentioned above, which noted that instrumentals had never been Everon's strong suit (a claim already contradicted at the time by the intro to "Venus" in 1997, as beautiful as anything by Dave Bainbridge), helps lighten the emotional load somewhat after bringing us to our knees. And Judith St�ber's enchanting voice on the ballad "Islanders" gently lifts us back up. And we stand tall as we listen to the glorious and energizing "Running", convinced that *North* is a truly ambitious album, a classic?and not just another heavy prog record?a formidable magnetic force that, while not reaching the absolute pinnacle of modern progressive rock, succeeds where so many others have failed, starting with Everon himself up to this point: to bring together in a single artistic work 10 crisp, simple, and clear melodies, set in 10 rings of precious metal, resting on 10 harmonic velvet cases. With the uncertain style of their early days having given way to a confident musical personality, Everon's music?that of their new album in particular?can fulfill the deepest progressive aspirations hidden within us. There's no doubt that *North* could give Everon the place it deserves: on the podium. At last!
items._genre: heavy prog / progressive rock / prog metal
items._cn_summary: 这是一支德国老牌前卫摇滚乐队2008年的专辑。北欧主题的同名曲在暴风雨之日写成，以伪弦乐编制营造哥特式厚重氛围。Oliver Philipps的嗓音被重点强调，被认为是乐队最大优势，从早期不够稳定到如今跻身顶级行列。开篇曲'Hands'旋律紧凑、键盘低调克制，拒绝虚饰繁复编制，体现返璞归真的意图。'A Brief Encounter'以原声吉他与钢琴构建，是向Yes致敬的意外惊喜之作。'Test of Time'则是华丽的前卫金属，短促大提琴前奏点睛。整体上，Everon被认为延续了Rush最具旋律性的传统，同时融合Vanden Plas的金属感和Sylvan的交响化倾向，试图在简单与恢弘之间寻找平衡点。

items.body: Eight tracks, two of them longer than eight minutes and one past eleven: Fields of the Nephilim built their third album around length. Beggars Banquet released “Elizium” on 24 September 1990, two years after “The Nephilim” had taken the gothic rock band from Stevenage to number 12 in the UK. The new album peaked at number 22. It turns 36 this year, and it remains the last studio record by the line-up of Carl McCoy, Tony Pettitt, Peter Yates, Paul Wright and Alexander “Nod” Wright. The band recorded “Elizium” in 1990 at Park Gate Studios in Battle, East Sussex, with additional recording and mixing at Astoria in Hampton Court. Andy Jackson, the engineer on Pink Floyd‘s late-1980s records, produced the album with the band and engineered the sessions; Jon Carin added keyboards. McCoy wrote the lyrics and the five members share the music credits. The title respells Elysium, the afterlife of Greek religion, and “At the Gates of Silent Memory” opens with the voice of Aleister Crowley reading from his poem “At Sea” in a 1920 recording. Beverley Carruthers shot the front sleeve, and Sheer Faith and Chris Bigg designed the packaging. ‘Elizium’ tracklist, singles and reissues The album runs 48 minutes and 3 seconds: “(Dead But Dreaming)”, “For Her Light”, “At the Gates of Silent Memory”, “(Paradise Regained)”, “Submission”, “Sumerland (What Dreams May Come)”, “Wail of Sumer” and “And There Will Your Heart Be Also”. Beggars Banquet issued it in the UK on LP, CD and cassette, with Rebel Rec. and SPV handling the German-speaking countries. “For Her Light” came out as the lead single in July 1990 and reached number 54 in the UK; “Sumerland (Dreamed Version)” followed in November 1990 and peaked at number 37. Music On Vinyl repressed the album on LP in 2011. Beggars Arkive marked the 30th anniversary on 11 December 2020 with a 180-gram dark green vinyl edition, and on 5 April 2024 released an expanded double LP on brick red vinyl. That edition spreads the album over three sides and adds four tracks on the fourth: “Sumerland (Single Version)”, “For Her Light (Two)”, “Submission Two (The Dub Posture)” and “Sumerland (Dreamed Version)”. John Dent handled the analogue transfer and Sean Magee cut the vinyl master. About Fields of the Nephilim Fields of the Nephilim formed in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, in 1984 around vocalist Carl McCoy, bassist Tony Pettitt, guitarist Paul Wright, drummer Alexander “Nod” Wright and saxophonist Gary Wisker. Peter Yates joined on guitar in 1985, the year the band released the “Burning the Fields” EP on its own Tower Release label. Jungle Records reissued it and financed the “Returning to Gehenna” EP in 1986. Situation Two, the Beggars Banquet imprint, signed the band in 1986 and released the singles “Power” and “Preacher Man” ahead of the debut album “Dawnrazor” in May 1987. The second album, “The Nephilim”, followed on 5 September 1988 and entered the UK chart at number 12, with “Moonchild” reaching number 28 as a single. The stand-alone single “Psychonaut” peaked at number 35 in May 1989, and the band moved up to the parent Beggars Banquet label for “Elizium” in September 1990. The two-night Festival of Fire at London’s Town & Country Club in 1991 produced the live album “Earth Inferno”, released on 25 March 1991, and the concert video “Visionary Heads”. McCoy left later that year. Pettitt, Yates and the Wright brothers continued as Rubicon with singer Andy Delaney, releasing “What Starts, Ends” in 1992 and “Room 101” in 1995, while McCoy formed Nefilim, whose only album “Zoon” appeared in 1996. McCoy and Pettitt announced a reunion at the Zillo Festival in Germany on 15 August 1998. Jungle Records issued the single “One More Nightmare (Trees Come Down)” in May 2000 and, in October 2002, the album “Fallen”, compiled from 1997 to 2001 recordings and disowned by the band as unauthorised. “Mourning Sun”, the first new Fields of the Nephilim studio album since “Elizium”, came out on 28 November 2005. A new line-up returned to the stage at the London Astoria in May 2007 and headlined M’era Luna in 2008. The double live album “Ceromonies (Ad Mortem Ad Vitam)”, recorded at Shepherd’s Bush Empire, appeared on McCoy’s Sacred Symphony label in April 2012, and the single “Prophecy” followed on 17 March 2016. Guitarist Tom Edwards, a member from 2008 to 2016, died in January 2017, as Side-Line reported in Fields of the Nephilim / Adam Ant guitarist Tom Edwards dies aged 41. Beggars Arkive has since reissued the Situation Two and Beggars Banquet catalogue: the 30th anniversary “Elizium” in December 2020, an expanded “The Nephilim” in October 2023, the four-track expanded “Elizium” in April 2024 and a remastered “Dawnrazor” in December 2025. McCoy and Pettitt lead the current line-up with guitarists Gavin King and Adam Leach. Thirty-six years after its release, “Elizium” closes the first chapter of that catalogue, the final album of the original five-piece before “Earth Inferno” documented its last shows.
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评以纪念性质梳理了Fields of the Nephilim第三张专辑《Elizium》发行36周年的相关信息，包括录音地点、制作团队、曲目列表及历年再版情况。文章侧重事实陈述而非音乐分析，涉及Andy Jackson制作、Jon Carin键盘参与、Aleister Crowley 1920年代朗读录音作为开场等制作细节。该乐队作为英国哥特摇滚代表，以神秘主义意象和宗教符号为创作主题，专辑标题取自希腊神话中的冥界乐土概念。对于关注暗潮与后朋克领域的听众而言，这是该流派发展史上的重要作品之一，但文章本身缺乏对音乐风格、声音设计或艺术创新的深入评述，更多偏向资讯整理性质。

items.body: Boston gothic post-punk and deathrock band Gossip Collar has released “Eaten of Worms”, its third full-length album, on September 4, 2026 through Bat-Cave Productions. The ten-track record is available on CD and LP through the label, with a digital edition on Bandcamp. Eaten Of Worms by Gossip Collar ‘Eaten of Worms’ tracklist and credits Eaten of Worms was recorded and mixed by Marc Valois at Dead Moon Audio in Somerville, Massachusetts, and mastered by Jeff Lipton at Peerless Mastering in Boston. The album’s ten tracks are: Disguise My Heart Scavengers Big Top Comes Crashing Down Haerisis Dead Thing Why Me? Peaceful In Daylight Spelling Misery Unsafe State Merchants Of The Wave The record pairs electronic textures with serrated guitar work, running through recurring images of water, predatory animals and religious dread across its ten songs. CD and LP copies can be ordered directly through Bat-Cave Productions, with a download code included. About Gossip Collar Gossip Collar formed in Boston in the dark basement scene at the tail end of the pandemic, bringing together members previously involved with The Showcase Showdown, Spitzz and Secret Hearts. The band’s lineup is Victoria on vocals and guitar, Tom on guitar, Mark on bass and Megan on drums. Gossip Collar released a self-titled debut album on April 7, 2023, followed by spinning silk for parasites on October 31, 2024. Eaten of Worms, out September 4, 2026 via Bat-Cave Productions, is the band’s third album. Gossip Collar has performed alongside The March Violets, Pink Turns Blue, Rendez-Vous, Haunt Me, House of Harm, Fotocrime and Sympathy Flowers. Eaten of Worms extends that catalogue with the band’s most recent studio work to date. Follow Gossip Collar: – Bandcamp – Instagram

items.body: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail has released “Vile Train”, a gothic rock single that previews the band’s fourth studio album, Infinite Fountain, due November 6, 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The song arrives with an official video directed and edited by Jean De Oliviera. ‘Vile Train’ single details “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago, with co-production by Night Nail in Berlin and additional vocals and guitar from VV & the Void. Frontman Brandon Robert said the track drew its initial inspiration from a visit to Pompeii, where a fresco depicting an angel and a demon in an embrace suggested “dark and brutal truths about love sung in a twisted but beautiful way.” The video reunites the band with director Jean De Oliviera, whose previous work with Night Nail includes “Hollow Day,” “Little Armenia” and “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher.” Shot in black and white, it cuts between Robert and bassist Ilija Gavrilenko performing among amplifiers and outdoor scenes set among stone arches and fountain basins. A full tracklist for Infinite Fountain has not been announced. The album also includes mixing and post-production work by Sven Wolff of Patenbrigade: Wolff. Night Nail plans to support the release with shows across the US, UK and Europe during 2026 and 2027. About Night Nail Night Nail formed in Los Angeles in 2013 and relocated to Berlin in 2018, the same year the band’s debut album, LA Demons, appeared on Cleopatra Records. March To Autumn followed in 2020 through Cold Transmission, and Fates Explained arrived on Metropolis Records in 2023, mixed and mastered by Pete Burns of Kill Shelter; Side-Line covered the single “Fates Explained” at the time. The band followed with the archival release Early Demons and Demos and the remix album Fates Remade in 2024, after earlier singles including “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher” and “Cracks In My Heart”, the latter featuring Luna De La Torre on vocals. Night Nail’s catalogue connects darkwave electronics with gothic rock’s appetite for emotional extremes, a combination built up over four albums and multiple labels since the band’s Los Angeles beginnings. “Vile Train” and the forthcoming Infinite Fountain, out on Icy Cold Records, mark the band’s next chapter and its first full-length since 2023’s Fates Explained. Follow Night Nail: – Bandcamp – Spotify – Website
